One-Hot Encode Categorical Covariates

oneHotEncode.Rd

Adds one-hot (dummy) columns for multi-level categorical covariates to a data frame, following the naming convention used across the Pharmetheus forest-plot tooling: <covariate><sep><level>, with the lowest level dropped as the reference unless stated otherwise.

It is the shared building block behind setupDfCovs() and the optional oneHot argument of getForestDFSCM() and getForestDFemp(), and it matches the columns produced by NONMEM FREM data sets and PMXFrem::createFREMModel().

Usage

oneHotEncode(
  data,
  spec,
  sep = "_",
  missVal = -99,
  includeReference = FALSE,
  imputeMissing = FALSE,
  dropOriginal = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the raw categorical columns.

spec

The covariates to encode, in one of two forms:

  • A character vector of column names. Each is encoded with its lowest non-missing level as the reference.

  • A named list. Each element is either NULL (lowest level as reference), a single value (used as the reference level), or a list with ref (reference level) and optional levels (the non-reference levels to create columns for; defaults to all remaining levels).

sep

The separator between the covariate name and the level in the new column names. Defaults to "_", matching the FREM convention. Changing it breaks alignment with FREM tooling and is discouraged.

missVal

The value indicating missing data. Rows holding missVal (or NA) in the raw column receive missVal in the dummy columns unless imputeMissing = TRUE. Defaults to -99.

includeReference

Logical. If TRUE, a dummy column is also created for the reference level. Defaults to FALSE.

imputeMissing

Logical. If TRUE, rows with a missing raw value are set to 0 in every dummy column (imputed to the reference category). If FALSE (default), they are set to missVal, so downstream code can keep treating them as missing.

dropOriginal

Logical. If TRUE, the raw categorical column is removed after its dummy columns have been added. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

data with the dummy columns added (numeric 0/1, or missVal on missing rows when imputeMissing = FALSE). If a COVARIATEGROUPS column is present it is moved back to the last position.

Details

For a covariate GENO with non-missing levels 1, 2, 3, 4 and the default reference (level 1), the function adds GENO_2, GENO_3, and GENO_4; the reference level is represented by all three being 0.

The function is idempotent: if a target column already exists it is left untouched when its non-missing rows agree with the requested encoding, and an error is raised when they do not. This makes it safe to call on data sets that already carry FREM dummy columns.

See also

setupDfCovs, getCovStats

Examples

dfData <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "SimVal/DAT-1-MI-PMX-2.csv", package = "PMXForest")
)
# One record per subject, a few categorical covariates
d <- dfData[!duplicated(dfData$ID), c("ID", "GENO", "RACE", "SEX")]

# Default: lowest level is the reference
head(oneHotEncode(d, spec = c("GENO", "RACE")))
#>     ID GENO RACE SEX GENO_2 GENO_3 GENO_4 RACE_2 RACE_3 RACE_4 RACE_5
#> 1    1    2    1   1      1      0      0      0      0      0      0
#> 27   7    2    1   1      1      0      0      0      0      0      0
#> 34  13    2    2   1      1      0      0      1      0      0      0
#> 60  19    4    1   1      0      0      1      0      0      0      0
#> 86  25    2    1   1      1      0      0      0      0      0      0
#> 112 31    3    1   1      0      1      0      0      0      0      0

# Explicit reference level for GENO (level 2), and drop the raw column
head(oneHotEncode(d, spec = list(GENO = list(ref = 2)), dropOriginal = TRUE))
#>     ID RACE SEX GENO_1 GENO_3 GENO_4
#> 1    1    1   1      0      0      0
#> 27   7    1   1      0      0      0
#> 34  13    2   1      0      0      0
#> 60  19    1   1      0      0      1
#> 86  25    1   1      0      0      0
#> 112 31    1   1      0      1      0

# "" separator -> GENO1, GENO2, ... (matching typical NONMEM indicator names)
head(oneHotEncode(d, spec = "GENO", sep = ""))
#>     ID GENO RACE SEX GENO2 GENO3 GENO4
#> 1    1    2    1   1     1     0     0
#> 27   7    2    1   1     1     0     0
#> 34  13    2    2   1     1     0     0
#> 60  19    4    1   1     0     0     1
#> 86  25    2    1   1     1     0     0
#> 112 31    3    1   1     0     1     0
